cves.summary: Zr.Admin.NET commit 1845017 through commit eb9228a contains a missing authorization vulnerability in TasksController.Get that allows any logged-in user to read scheduled task details without the monitor:job permission. Attackers can obtain task ids from the unprotected /monitor/jobLog/list endpoint and retrieve job parameters, API URLs, cron expressions, and stored SQL statements.

A flaw has been found in D-Link DIR-600L 2.17b02. Affected by this issue is the function hnap_main of the file htdocs/cgibin of the component HNAP Handler. Executing a manipulation can lead to stack-based buffer overflow. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used.

Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 in assign_headers() can lead to RCE.

This issue affects Apache HTTP Server: from 2.4.55 through 2.4.70.
Affected releases of mod_h2 from GitHub: from 2.0.8 through 2.0.42.

A vulnerability was found in vllm-project vllm 0.30.0/0.31.0. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file single_type_kv_cache_manager.py of the component Common Prefix Handler. The manipulation results in race condition. The attack may be performed from remote. Attacks of this nature are highly complex. It is stated that the exploitability is difficult. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 0.32.0 is able to resolve this issue. The patch is identified as e687a251bb056fa527846633f7a1b0a6c0f42374. You should upgrade the affected component.

A vulnerability has been found in sigoden dufs up to 0.46.0. This affects an unknown part of the file src/server.rs of the component WebDAV COPY Operation Handler. The manipulation leads to incorrect authorization. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. Upgrading to version 0.47.0 is able to mitigate this issue. The identifier of the patch is fba13dffb9c65b5e5e26419f64de709200277a04. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component.

A security vulnerability has been detected in TRENDnet TEW-657BRM 1.00.1. This vulnerability affects the function sprintf of the file /setup.cgi of the component mini_httpd. Such manipulation leads to out-of-bounds write. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The vendor explains: ""I am not able to confirm if such vulnerability exists as the product has been EOL for more than 15 years. We will send out an announcement letting customers know." This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

A vulnerability was detected in D-Link DIR-600L 2.17/2.17b02. Affected by this vulnerability is the function authenticationcgi_main of the file authentication.cgi. Performing a manipulation of the argument id/password results in stack-based buffer overflow. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit is now public and may be used.

Dancer versions before 1.3400 for Perl pass unvalidated session ids from the session cookie to the session engine.

read_session_id returns the cookie value as the session id without checking its characters, and Dancer hands it to the session engine to load the session.

A remote attacker may cause path traversal or injection in a session engine that uses the id in a file path, cache command or query without checking it.

A vulnerability was detected in TRENDnet TEW-657BRM 1.00.1. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file /usr/sbin/upgrade_flash.cgi. Performing a manipulation of the argument boundary results in stack-based buffer overflow. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The vendor explains: ""I am not able to confirm if such vulnerability exists as the product has been EOL for more than 15 years. We will send out an announcement letting customers know."

Hickory DNS hickory-proto 0.25.0-alpha.3 through 0.25.2 and hickory-net 0.26.0-alpha.1 before 0.26.2 contain a DNSSEC validation flaw in DnssecDnsHandle that accepts NSEC3-signed NODATA responses for zone-apex queries as secure without an NSEC3 record matching the hashed QNAME. On-path attackers or malicious authoritative servers can replay a validly signed non-apex NSEC3 with the zone's signed SOA to serve an authenticated (AD=1) denial of any apex RRtype for the negative-cache TTL.

The validating recursor in Hickory DNS hickory-recursor 0.25.0 through 0.26.0-alpha.1, hickory-resolver 0.26.0-alpha.1 before 0.26.2, and hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 caches DNSSEC-bogus answers using the untrusted, attacker-supplied record TTL (capped at 24 hours) instead of a short validation-failure TTL. A remote attacker who spoofs a single authoritative response with an invalid signature and a long TTL can keep the bogus result cached for up to 24 hours.

Hickory DNS hickory-proto 0.25.0 through 0.26.0-alpha.1 and hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 invert the relational operators in the wrap-around branch of find_covering_record() in nsec3.rs, so the last NSEC3 record in a zone's hash ring covers every hash except its owner. Attackers able to inject DNS responses can replay that NSEC3 record and its RRSIG to forge DNSSEC-validated negative responses denying legitimate names.

Hickory DNS hickory-proto through 0.26.0-alpha.1 and hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 contain a DNSSEC validation flaw in the validating recursor's NSEC handler that accepts parent-side ancestor-delegation NSEC records as proof of nonexistence for names below the zone cut. An on-path attacker, rogue parent nameserver, or attacker winning a port and TXID race can deliver one forged NXDOMAIN response built from genuinely signed parent NSEC records, causing authenticated denial of existing child-zone names cached for the negative TTL.

Hickory DNS hickory-proto 0.25.0-alpha.1 through 0.26.0-alpha.1 and hickory-net before 0.26.2 contain a logic bug in DnssecDnsHandle's DS-fetch path that caches transient DS lookup errors as Bogus DNSSEC validation verdicts. An attacker who induces a SERVFAIL, REFUSED, or timeout response to a child-zone DS sub-query causes the validator to return SERVFAIL for all names under that zone until the cache entry's TTL expires.

DNSSEC validation in Hickory DNS hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 and hickory-proto through 0.26.0-alpha.1 does not distinguish NODATA responses from wildcard-expanded positive responses. For a query that should return NODATA in a zone with wildcard records, an attacker can combine an NSEC3 record matching the query name with a signed wildcard record into a bogus positive response that validation accepts.

Hickory DNS hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 and hickory-proto through 0.26.0-alpha.1 perform insufficient checks on NSEC3 record names during DNSSEC verification, comparing only the hashed label without confirming the record belongs to the correct zone. Attackers can supply NSEC3 records from another zone with a matching hash label to forge DNSSEC nonexistence proofs.

The hickory-net crate in Hickory DNS 0.26.0 before 0.26.2 stops listening and returns an error when a client UDP connection receives a datagram that cannot be parsed as a DNS message. Remote attackers who guess the query's source port, without knowing the transaction ID, can spoof malformed responses to abort client queries, causing denial of service.

The hickory-resolver component of Hickory DNS 0.25.0 before 0.26.2 follows irrelevant CNAME records when resolving recursive queries, sending queries that are unnecessary to answer the original request. Attackers controlling DNS responses can include CNAME records in the authority or additional sections, or outside the original query name's CNAME chain, causing excess resolver queries and increased query amplification.

The validating recursive resolver and validating forwarder in Hickory DNS (hickory-server) 0.25.0 before 0.26.2 do not check whether the SOA record passed DNSSEC validation when assembling NXDOMAIN or NODATA responses. An attacker able to supply forged DNS responses can have a forged SOA record returned to clients with the AD bit set, misleading clients that rely on the server's DNSSEC validation.

The recursive resolver in Hickory DNS (all versions of the hickory-recursor crate, and hickory-resolver 0.26.0 before 0.26.2) caches an empty connection pool when it follows a referral with no glue records and all queries for the name servers' IP addresses fail. An attacker able to spoof DNS responses can make these lookups fail, causing all subsequent queries for the affected zone to fail until the cache entry expires or is evicted.

The DNS-over-QUIC (DoQ) server in hickory-server (hickory-dns) before 0.26.2 does not apply any timeout when reading a request message from a QUIC stream, bypassing all configured timeouts. A remote unauthenticated client can open a connection and a request stream and hold it open indefinitely, consuming server resources and causing a denial of service.

The hickory-net crate in Hickory DNS 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 allows DNSSEC validation bypass because Name's Hash ignores label lengths and ValidationCacheKey compares only that hash. An attacker controlling an unsigned delegation whose name differs from a signed target only in dot positions can prime an Insecure verdict, causing forged answers for the target to skip signature verification instead of returning SERVFAIL.

Hickory DNS hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 and hickory-proto 0.24.0 through 0.26.0-alpha.1 compare DNSKEY public keys against DNSSEC trust anchors without checking the DNSKEY record name, so an RRset made up only of trusted keys is accepted without RRSIG verification. Attackers able to spoof or control name server responses can replace a secure zone's DNSKEY RRset with the root zone's keys, and use a large TTL to keep it cached.

Hickory DNS hickory-proto through 0.26.0-alpha.1 and hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 contain an NSEC validation flaw that returns a secure proof for NXDOMAIN responses when the covering NSEC's Next Domain Name is a strict descendant of the query name, which actually proves the name exists as an empty non-terminal. On-path attackers can flip the unsigned rcode of a genuine signed NODATA response from NOERROR to NXDOMAIN, causing validators to accept forged nonexistence of the name.

Hickory DNS 0.25.0-alpha.3 through 0.25.2 contains a query amplification vulnerability in its recursive resolver, which mishandles cyclic sibling name server referrals that lack glue records. Attackers controlling two zones whose name servers reference each other without glue records can make the recursor loop, sending many upstream queries, amplified further by zero-TTL NS records.

Hickory DNS hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 and hickory-proto through 0.26.0-alpha.1 accept NSEC and NSEC3 records for DNSSEC nonexistence proofs when any other record with the same owner name passes signature validation. Attackers able to supply DNS responses can mix validly signed records with bogus same-name NSEC or NSEC3 records of different types in the authority section to forge nonexistence proofs.

The recursive resolver in Hickory DNS hickory-recursor 0.25.0 through 0.25.2 and hickory-resolver 0.26.0 before 0.26.2 does not apply out-of-bailiwick filtering to negative responses. Attackers able to supply crafted negative responses can include out-of-bailiwick records to facilitate cache poisoning and more easily exploit other DNSSEC verification flaws.

### Summary
AdminNeo v5.4.1 gets the latest version from GitHub API in a browser JavaScript function. Version number is then sent by POST request to `?script=version`. This endpoint lacks origin validation and accepts POST data from any source. An attacker can POST `version[]` parameter which PHP converts to an array. On next page load, function `rawurlencode()` receives this array instead of string and throws `TypeError`, returning HTTP 500 to all users for the next 24 hours.

Originally reported by @JoyGhoshs in Adminer: https://github.com/vrana/adminer/security/advisories/GHSA-q4f2-39gr-45jh
Although the version checking process was modified in AdminNeo, the root cause persisted.

### Workaround
If you can't upgrade, make the file `adminneo.version` in temp directory (usually the value of [upload_tmp_dir](https://www.php.net/ini.core#ini.upload-tmp-dir)) unwritable by web server.

### Details
#### 1. Intended design of `?script=version`
The endpoint is designed to receive version data from GitHub via browser JavaScript.
- `functions.js` line 110-121: Receives the latest release information from GitHub API by AJAX.
- JavaScript POSTs version number to `?script=version`.
- Server stores version number in `/tmp/adminneo.version` file that is used as a shared cache for all users in the same server for the next 24 hours.

```js
// function.js lines 119-120
const data = 'version=' + version + '&token=' + token;
ajax(baseUrl + 'script=version', null, data);
```

#### 2. The vulnerability

The endpoint only checks `$_GET["script"] == "version"` - it does not validate:
- Request origin (CSRF token is present, but not checked for this endpoint)
- Request source (any HTTP client can POST)
- Parameter types (`version` expected as string, array not rejected)

```php
// bootstrap.inc.php lines 44-53
if ($_GET["script"] == "version") {
	$filename = get_temp_dir() . "/adminneo.version";
	@unlink($filename); // It may not be writable by us, @ - it may not exist.

	$file = open_file_with_lock($filename);
	if ($file) {
		write_and_unlock_file($file, serialize(["version" => $_POST["version"]]));
	}
	exit;
}
```

#### 3. Type confusion crash
When POST contains `version[]` instead of `version`, PHP creates an array. When AdminNeo reads this file and passes to `cookie()` and then to `rawurlencode()`:

```php
// design.inc.php line 40
cookie("neo_version", $data["version"], $lifetime); // Sync expiration with the file.

// functions.inc.php lines 398-405
function cookie(string $name, string $value, int $lifetime = 2592000): void
{
	header("Set-Cookie: $name=" . rawurlencode($value)
		. ($lifetime ? "; expires=" . gmdate("D, d M Y H:i:s", time() + $lifetime) . " GMT" : "")
		. "; path=" . preg_replace('~\?.*~', '', $_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"])
		. (HTTPS ? "; secure" : "")
		. "; HttpOnly; SameSite=lax",
		false);
}
```

PHP 8.x throws:

```
Fatal error: Uncaught TypeError: rawurlencode(): Argument #1 ($string) must be of type string, array given
```

### Steps to Reproduce

(Example URL is for the official AdminNeo Docker image.)

**Step 1:** Verify AdminNeo is running and accessible.

```sh
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080
```

Expected output:

```
200
```

**Step 2:** Send the malicious POST request. The `version[]` syntax causes PHP to create an array instead of a string.

```sh
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080?script=version" -d "version[]=INJECTED"
```

Expected output: Empty response (no error).

**Step 3:** Access Adminer again to trigger the crash.

```sh
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080
```

Expected output:

```
500
```

**Step 4:** (Optional) View the PHP error in server logs.

```
Fatal error: Uncaught TypeError: rawurlencode(): Argument #1 ($string) must be of type string, array given
```

**Step 5:** (Optional) Inspect the poisoned file.

```sh
cat /tmp/adminneo.version
```

Expected output:

```
a:1:{s:7:"version";a:1:{i:0;s:8:"INJECTED";}}
```

**Recovery:**

```sh
rm /tmp/adminer.version
```

After deletion, AdminNeo returns HTTP 200.

<hr>

### Impact

**Type:** Denial of Service

**Root cause:** The `?script=version` endpoint is designed to receive data from GitHub via JavaScript, but lacks server-side validation. Any HTTP client can POST directly to this endpoint. Combined with missing type validation before `rawurlencode()`, this allows DoS for the next 24 hours.

**Affected users:** Any AdminNeo instance accessible over the network.
Multiple SQL injection vulnerabilities in index.php in Subjects 2.0 Postnuke module allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands via the (1) pageid, (2) subid, or (3) catid parameters.

Off-by-one error in the xlog function of mountd in the Linux NFS utils package (nfs-utils) before 1.0.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary code via certain RPC requests to mountd that do not contain newlines.

### Summary

The JLine3 built-in `grep` command wraps the user-supplied regular expression with
`.*` before compiling it with Java's backtracking regex engine. This amplifies
catastrophic backtracking and allows a short pattern such as `(a+)+b` to hang the
command thread on non-matching input. In environments that expose the JLine shell to
remote users, this is a denial-of-service issue.

### Details

In `builtins/src/main/java/org/jline/builtins/PosixCommands.java`, the grep
implementation rewrites the user pattern before compilation:

```java
String regex = args.remove(0);
String regexp = regex;
if (opt.isSet("word-regexp")) {
    regexp = "\\b" + regexp + "\\b";
}
if (opt.isSet("line-regexp")) {
    regexp = "^" + regexp + "$";
} else {
    regexp = ".*" + regexp + ".*";
}
```

The transformed pattern is compiled with `Pattern.compile(...)` and then used to test
each input line. For a payload such as `(a+)+b`, the automatic `.*` prefix and suffix
increase the backtracking search space substantially.

Affected source location:
- `builtins/src/main/java/org/jline/builtins/PosixCommands.java`
- `grep(...)`

### PoC

1. Create a file containing a long run of `a` characters:

```sh
printf 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa\n' > /tmp/testfile.txt
```

2. Run JLine3's built-in `grep` against that file:

```sh
grep '(a+)+b' /tmp/testfile.txt
```

Expected result:
- The command stops responding.
- The executing thread consumes high CPU.

Reproduction environment:
- JLine3 on x86_64 Linux
- OpenJDK 25.0.2

### Impact

This is a denial-of-service vulnerability caused by catastrophic regex backtracking.
Any application embedding `org.jline:jline-builtins` and exposing the built-in `grep`
command is impacted. In remote shell deployments, an attacker can occupy a worker
thread indefinitely and repeat the attack across multiple sessions to reduce service
availability for other users.

### Suggested Fix

The preferred fix for the current git head is:
- stop rewriting non-line-regexp searches as `.*...*`
- use `Matcher.find()` for substring semantics
- compile user patterns with a linear-time engine such as RE2/J

Suggested patch:

```diff
diff --git a/builtins/pom.xml b/builtins/pom.xml
a/builtins/pom.xml
+++ b/builtins/pom.xml
@@
         <dependency>
+            <groupId>com.google.re2j</groupId>
+            <artifactId>re2j</artifactId>
+            <version>1.8</version>
+        </dependency>
+        <dependency>
             <groupId>org.jline</groupId>
             <artifactId>jline-reader</artifactId>
         </dependency>

diff --git a/builtins/src/main/java/org/jline/builtins/PosixCommands.java b/builtins/src/main/java/org/jline/builtins/PosixCommands.java
a/builtins/src/main/java/org/jline/builtins/PosixCommands.java
+++ b/builtins/src/main/java/org/jline/builtins/PosixCommands.java
@@
-import java.util.regex.Pattern;
+import com.google.re2j.Pattern;
@@
         if (opt.isSet("line-regexp")) {
             regexp = "^" + regexp + "$";
-        } else {
-            regexp = ".*" + regexp + ".*";
         }
@@
-        boolean m = p.matcher(line).matches();
+        boolean m = opt.isSet("line-regexp")
+                ? p.matcher(line).matches()
+                : p.matcher(line).find();
```

### Credits

This issue was identified by Michał Majchrowicz and Marcin Wyczechowski, members of the AFINE Team.

### Summary
The `PATCH /api/settings` endpoint writes the entire request body to persistent settings without a field whitelist. An authenticated user can set security-critical fields that are not meant to be modifiable here — notably `requireLogin`. Setting `requireLogin: false` disables authentication for the whole application, exposing all protected routes (e.g. `/api/keys`, `/api/providers`) to unauthenticated access.

### Details
Root cause is unfiltered mass assignment (CWE-915):

- `src/app/api/settings/route.js` (PATCH handler) parses the body and passes it to `updateSettings(body)`, with special handling only for `newPassword` and `oidcClientSecret`. All other fields pass through.
- `src/lib/db/repos/settingsRepo.js` — `updateSettings` does `next = { ...current, ...updates }`, so any key in the body overwrites stored settings, including `requireLogin`, `tunnelDashboardAccess`, `authMode`.
- `src/dashboardGuard.js` — `isAuthenticated` returns `true` whenever `settings.requireLogin === false`, bypassing auth on all protected routes.

This is distinct from CVE-2026-5842 (CWE-285, pre-auth bypass on `/api`, patched in 0.3.75). This finding requires a valid authenticated session and abuses input handling, not missing authentication.

### PoC
Instance on `localhost:20128`, default password `123456`.

1. Authenticate, capture session:
   `POST /api/auth/login` body `{"password":"123456"}` → `200 {"success":true}`
2. Mass-assign with the authenticated session:
   `PATCH /api/settings` body `{"requireLogin":false}` → `200`, response confirms `"requireLogin":false`
3. Verify bypass with NO session/credentials:
   `GET /api/keys` → `200`, returns full API key list unauthenticated
4. Cleanup (authenticated): `PATCH /api/settings` body `{"requireLogin":true}` → `GET /api/keys` returns `401` again

### Impact
Post-authentication mass assignment. Any authenticated user (including one using the default password) can disable authentication globally, then read all stored API keys and provider connection data without credentials, and toggle tunnel/dashboard exposure. Escalates to remote full compromise when chained with the default password `123456` on an instance exposed via tunnel (`tunnelDashboardAccess` defaults to `true`).

### Suggested fix
Whitelist user-configurable fields in the PATCH handler; move security-critical fields (`requireLogin`, `tunnelDashboardAccess`, `authMode`) to a dedicated endpoint requiring re-authentication (current-password re-entry), mirroring the existing DB export/import re-auth flow.

cwe.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

cves.summary: The Windows Internet Naming Service (WINS) for Microsoft Windows Server 2003, and possibly Windows NT and Server 2000, does not properly validate the length of certain packets, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary code.
mod_digest for Apache before 1.3.31 does not properly verify the nonce of a client response by using a AuthNonce secret.
Unknown vulnerability in the mail command handler in Mailman before 2.0.14 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via malformed e-mail commands.
IMail IMONITOR status.cgi CGI script allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service with many calls to status.cgi.
Network HotSync program in Handspring Visor does not have authentication, which allows remote attackers to retrieve email and files.
Buffer overflow in KaZaA Media Desktop 2.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) and possibly execute arbitrary code via a response to the ad server.

APC Web/SNMP Management Card prior to Firmware 310 only supports one telnet connection, which allows a remote attacker to create a denial of service via repeated failed logon attempts which temporarily locks the card.
Digital Creations Zope 2.3.1 b1 and earlier allows a local attacker (Zope user) with through-the-web scripting capabilities to alter ZClasses class attributes.
Internet Explorer 5.0 allows window spoofing, allowing a remote attacker to spoof a legitimate web site and capture information from the client.

Multiple cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in the primary and management web interfaces in Netegrity IdentityMinder Web Edition 5.6 allows remote attackers to execute script as other users via (1) script that starts with %00 in the numOfExpressions parameter or (2) the mobjtype parameter.
Buffer overflow in passwd in BSD based operating systems 4.3 and earlier allows local users to gain root privileges by specifying a long shell or GECOS field.
Vulnerability in the Wguest CGI program.
webdist CGI program (webdist.cgi) in SGI IRIX allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via shell metacharacters in the distloc parameter.
IRIX fam service allows an attacker to obtain a list of all files on the server.
periodic in FreeBSD 4.1.1 and earlier, and possibly other operating systems, allows local users to overwrite arbitrary files via a symlink attack.
The presence of the Distributed GL Daemon (dgld) service on port 5232 on SGI IRIX systems allows remote attackers to identify the target host as an SGI system.
MailMan Webmail 3.0.25 and earlier allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via shell metacharacters in the alternate_template parameter.
